question: Which of the following Constitutions inspired the law-making process in India?
solution:
The correct answer is __**British Constitution**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The British Constitution inspired the law-making process in India. The Indian Constitution borrowed many features from the British Constitution, including:
 
• Parliamentary system
 
• The concept of a sovereign Parliament, with a division into two houses, the Rajya Sabha (Upper House) and the Lok Sabha (Lower House)
 
• Rule of law
 
• The principle of equality before the law and protection of individual rights
 
• Legislative procedures
 
• The procedures for passing bills and conducting debates in the Indian Parliament
 
• Single citizenship
 
• The concept that individuals hold citizenship of the country as a whole, not specific states or regions
